theme: I will sing of the steadfast love of the LORD
readingInstruction: Read Psalm 89:1-37. The first half of the psalm celebrates God’s covenant with David. It is a magnificent statement of confidence. Keep in mind that the second half of the psalm (verses 38-52), which comes later in the plan, brings a painful question.
settingTheScene: Psalm 89 is a Maskil of Ethan the Ezrahite and the last psalm of Book 3. It was probably written after the Babylonian exile began, when the Davidic king had been taken captive. Yet the first thirty-seven verses are full of praise for the covenant God made with David in 2 Samuel 7. It is placed here in Unit 12 as a bridge between Isaiah’s promises of a coming king and the later crisis. Verses 38 to 52 appear in Unit 13.
observation: “I will sing of the steadfast love of the LORD, forever; with my mouth I will make known your faithfulness to all generations” (v. 1).
“For I said, Steadfast love will be built up forever; in the heavens you will establish your faithfulness” (v. 2).
“You have said, I have made a covenant with my chosen one; I have sworn to David my servant” (v. 3).
“Who in the skies can be compared to the LORD? Who among the heavenly beings is like the LORD?” (v. 6).
“Blessed are the people who know the festal shout, who walk, O LORD, in the light of your face” (v. 15).
“I have found David, my servant; with my holy oil I have anointed him” (v. 20).
“He shall cry to me, You are my Father, my God, and the Rock of my salvation” (v. 26).
“I will not violate my covenant or alter the word that went forth from my lips” (v. 34).
interpretation:
The psalm begins with the word “steadfast love” and “faithfulness,” repeated throughout. These two words are used seven times in the first part of the psalm. The psalmist makes a vow: he will sing of them forever. His confidence rests on what God has said and sworn. God’s love is not a feeling that fluctuates but a covenant that stands.

The first section praises God as the creator and ruler. The heavens praise his wonders. No one is like him. He rules the raging sea, stills its waves, and crushed Rahab, the sea monster. North and south, Tabor and Hermon, all belong to him. And such a God is not distant. Blessed are those who walk in the light of his face.

The second part, verses 19 to 37, recalls the covenant with David in detail. God chose David from among the people, anointed him, strengthened him. He promised that David would call him Father, and that God would make him the firstborn, “the highest of the kings of the earth.” His line would endure as long as the heavens. Even if his sons sin, God says, “I will punish their transgression with the rod,” but “I will not remove from him my steadfast love.” Then the oath: “Once for all I have sworn by my holiness; I will not lie to David.”

Why does this matter in Unit 12? Because Isaiah’s promises of a child, a shoot of Jesse, and a servant all depend on the covenant with David. The psalm is the legal basis for hope. When Judah’s kingdom is threatened, this is what the faithful return to: God has sworn, and he will not lie.

The psalm’s second half asks, “But now you have cast off and rejected.” The painful tension between promise and experience is what the Old Testament waits for Christ to resolve.
connection: Luke 1:32-33 says that the angel told Mary her son would be given the throne of his father David. Acts 13:22-23 says God raised up from David’s offspring a Savior, Jesus. Hebrews 1:5 uses 2 Samuel 7 to say “I will be to him a father.” Colossians 1:18 calls Jesus “the firstborn of all creation” and “the firstborn from the dead.” Revelation 1:5 calls him “the ruler of kings on earth.” Romans 15:8 says Christ confirmed the promises given to the patriarchs.
application:
Choose to sing, or read aloud, Psalm 89:1 as a vow to make known God’s faithfulness.

Think about one promise of God that you are holding on to. Write down the verse and what it says.

Thank God that his covenant is not broken by our failure, because Christ has fulfilled it.
prayerPrompts: Sing of God’s steadfast love in your own words.
Thank him for his sworn promise to David.
Ask him to make known his faithfulness to those who come after you.
